name: Project Change Management Plan
one_liner: How changes to the baselined project are raised, assessed, approved and controlled.
purpose: Defines and documents the change process for the project: the activities, roles and responsibilities related to identifying, documenting, assessing, approving, prioritising, implementing, controlling and communicating requested project changes. It brings transparency, accountability and traceability to all changes made after the project scope and plans have been baselined. Its escalation procedure ensures that changes with significant impact on project performance are assessed and approved by the appropriate level of authority.

fields.what: States the purpose: describe the change management process for the project, define change-related roles and responsibilities, and specify the methodology, standards, tools and techniques used.
fields.castor: Change management for Project CASTOR after the 26 Jun 2026 baseline.

fields.what: Bring transparency, accountability and traceability to all changes made after scope and plans are baselined, so significant impacts on scope, time, cost, quality or risk are properly approved.
fields.castor: No change to the €8.4 m budget or the 15 May 2028 go-live without a PSC decision.

fields.f: What is considered a project change
fields.what: A change can result from a scope change, a new requirement, an identified issue, a preventive action to reduce a risk level, or a decision altering any baseline.
fields.castor: Scope, schedule, cost, quality and Levallois contract baselines are all change-controlled.

fields.what: Managing changes to configuration items — project artefacts and deliverables and their versions — is part of quality management and is documented in the Quality Management Plan.
fields.castor: Document versioning handled by W. Edwards Deming (PQA) under the Quality Management Plan.

fields.what: Any stakeholder can request a change at any time. The PM registers it in the Change Log and ensures it is described on a Change Request Form.
fields.castor: Verbal cabinet request of 21 Sep 2027 written up and logged as CHG-011 on 23 Sep.

fields.f: Step 2: Change Assessment and Action Recommendation
fields.what: Assess whether it really is a project change, define options, size each option by impact on objectives, quality, risk, schedule, cost, effort and contract, then set priority.
fields.who: PM leads · PCT estimates · BM and SP consulted
fields.castor: CHG-011 sized at +€310k and +8 weeks on the Release 2 integration stream.

fields.what: If a contractor is involved, the impact on the contract must be assessed: contract changes are costly and slow, and their volume may be constrained by European tendering rules.
fields.castor: Any change touching the Levallois contract of 18 Sep 2026 needs Legal review first.

fields.what: Decision taken by the appropriate decision-makers per the escalation procedure. Four possible decisions: Approve, Reject, Postpone or Merge. Requests needing clarification return to Step 2.
fields.who: PO or PSC decides · PM communicates
fields.castor: PSC of 12 Oct 2027 postponed CHG-011 until the Treaty reform enters into force.

fields.what: For approved or merged changes the PM incorporates the actions into the Project Work Plan and updates plans, logs and checklists — requirements, quality, resource, acceptance, and all four logs.
fields.castor: Approved changes become numbered Work Plan tasks before the next status report.

fields.what: Monitor and control changes so they can be communicated to each decision layer; the PM collects change information and controls the status of every change management activity.
fields.castor: Change Log reviewed at the weekly Project Status Meeting each Tuesday.

fields.what: PSC consulted on approvals and informed monthly; PO accountable and approves, rejects or escalates; BM and SP consulted from requester and provider sides; PM responsible; PCT supports; BIG informed.
fields.castor: Florence Nightingale accountable; Grace Hopper and Leonardo da Vinci consulted on every assessment.

fields.f: Change Control Board (CCB) / Change Advisory Board (CAB)
fields.what: The PO and/or PSC may delegate the authority for approving or rejecting changes to a Change Control Board or Change Advisory Board; in the template the PSC plays that role.
fields.who: PO/PSC delegate · PM services the board
fields.castor: No separate board: the CASTOR PSC acts as Change Control Board.

fields.what: Two rows: the Plan itself (I, I, A, C, I, I, R, I) and the Manage Project Changes process (I, C, A, S, I, I, R, C).
fields.castor: PSC only Informed on the plan, but Consulted once changes are being managed.

fields.what: Lists the techniques used for change management — principally impact analysis — and the tools: the Change Log and the Change Request Form.
fields.castor: Impact analysis, risk analysis, Change Log, Change Request Form.

fields.what: Four blocks: identification and description; assessment and action description; approval; implementation. Customise scales of urgency, size and priority to the project.
fields.castor: PM² Change Log used unchanged; stored beside the Risk, Issue and Decision Logs.

fields.what: Submitted, Assessing, Waiting for Approval, Approved, Rejected, Postponed, Merged (folded into another change), Implemented (work incorporated in the Project Work Plan).
fields.castor: CHG-011 ran Submitted → Assessing → Waiting for Approval → Postponed.

fields.what: Size is the effort required to implement the change; Priority is its agreed relative importance. Both use 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low.
fields.castor: CHG-011: Size 4 (High), Priority 2 (Low) — high effort, low urgency.

fields.what: Captures the original request: project name, Change ID, change name, identification date, requestor, category, priority, current situation, desired situation, impact/risks of not implementing, out of scope, links.
fields.castor: CR-011 signed off by the requesting cabinet before assessment started.

fields.what: Changes surface from team brainstorming, meetings, user feedback, a risk response, a major delay or cost overrun, assumptions analysis, or a direct stakeholder request.
fields.castor: Weekly status meeting and monthly PSC are the two standing identification points.

fields.what: Issues of significant size may lead to a project change, so issues are often linked to change items; both are logged, assessed, assigned and tracked, each in its own log.
fields.castor: ISS-012 (architect resignation) linked to the Release 2 replanning entry.

fields.f: 7. Change Assessment and Action Recommendation Activities
fields.what: Names the assessment activities and tools: impact analysis on time, cost and quality; risk analysis for new risks; Risk Log; Change Log. Reviewed at Change Control Meetings.
fields.who: PM runs · PCT and BM contribute
fields.castor: Impact analysis by Nikola Tesla; new risk raised on the Release 2 date.

fields.what: The meeting where changes are reviewed, recommendations proposed, prioritised and logged. Minor changes may be first discussed at the more frequent Project Status Meeting.
fields.castor: Monthly Change Control Meeting held the week before each PSC.

fields.what: Significant-size changes are discussed at the monthly PSC. For substantial scope, schedule or cost changes the PSC re-checks the Project Charter boundaries and the Business Case justification.
fields.castor: CHG-011 tested against the Charter scope statement before the PSC voted.

fields.what: Very Low and Low size changes are approved at the Managing Layer (BM and PM); Medium, High and Very High by the PSC or CCB/CAB, which escalates further.
fields.who: PM applies · PO owns the rule
fields.castor: Managing Layer may approve only changes with no impact on €8.4 m or committed dates.

fields.what: Substantial project scope changes are reported yearly in the Project Progress Report, to be reviewed and approved by the Appropriate Governance Body.
fields.castor: Reported yearly to the Corporate Investment Board chaired by Lorenzo de' Medici.

fields.what: Records where implementation of approved changes is reflected, monitored and controlled: the Project Work Plan, the Change Log and the Decision Log.
fields.castor: CHG-011 traced to DEC-011 in the Decision Log and to REQ-108.

fields.what: New or open changes are reassessed weekly at Project Status Meetings; Medium, High and Very High changes are reported monthly to the PSC and CCB/CAB, yearly to governance bodies.
fields.castor: Change Log extract in every monthly PSC pack from Jul 2026 onwards.

fields.what: Cross-references the Project Handbook (escalation), Communications Management Plan (who is told what), Quality Management Plan (configuration) and Issue Management Plan (issues that generate changes).
fields.castor: Handbook, Communications, Quality and Issue plans, all version 1.0 of 26 Jun 2026.

fields.what: Lists each reference or related document by title, version, date and source or link/location.
fields.castor: 26.Change_Log.CASTOR.xlsx in the ESM PSO project folder.

traps: Four decisions exist: Approve, Reject, Postpone, Merge — not just approve or reject.
The plan defines the process; the Change Log holds the actual change instances.
Change Log is set up in Planning; Risk, Issue and Decision Logs in Initiating.
Versioning artefacts is configuration/quality management, not project change management.
A verbal request is not a change until it has a Change Request Form and Log entry.
